_note: Runtime transform vocabulary recovered from Scaler 3's binary string tables (parameter ids + enum labels). These are the knobs applied ON TOP of a baked expression pattern at playback time. Values are the option labels as they appear in the UI; numeric ranges are not recoverable from strings alone.

arpeggio._patternsNote: 'Up' is inferred as the default first entry; the string table starts at 'Down'. Thumb/Pinky variants pin the lowest/highest voice as a pedal while the rest of the chord cycles.
arpeggio._ratesNote: d = dotted (x1.5), t = triplet (x2/3). '1/2' and '1/4' plain entries exist in the UI; the table stores the modified forms adjacently.

humanize._note: Runtime humanize is a swing/quantize pass with a depth (amount) and a rate multiplier (timing). It is NOT the source of the micro-timing already baked into the shipped patterns - the library patterns ship with position_offset/duration_offset all zero and their feel encoded directly in 'position'.

voicingProfile._note: How a pattern's abstract noteIndex ladder is realised as concrete pitches on the target chord. This is the missing link between an index-based pattern and actual MIDI notes.

keysLock._note: Maps incoming played keys onto legal notes - the mechanic that makes 'you cannot play a wrong note' work.

rotate.rotate_increment: steps to rotate the pattern by each cycle
